requirements.text: Never bump the major version unless explicitly told to by the maintainer. Multiple backward-incompatible changes may be batched into a single major release.

Minor version bumps are reserved for new major features and backward-incompatible changes such as API breaks or removed commands. Everything else - bugfixes, dashboards, refactors - only bumps the build number.
All four binaries (cloche, cloched, cloche-agent, clo) share a single version string sourced from internal/version/VERSION.
A release is prepared by running the changelog host workflow before tagging; re-running it replaces the top entry for the same version rather than stacking duplicates.
Releases are annotated git tags v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<BUILD> on main, with the CHANGELOG entry as the tag message and a GitHub Release created via gh.
Release rehearsals must use CLOCHE_RELEASE_DRY_RUN=1; the local tag it creates must be deleted before the real run.

Domain logic must stay independent of infrastructure: ports define interfaces like ContainerRuntime, RunStore, and AgentAdapter; adapters implement them. New integrations go in internal/adapters and are never imported by domain code.
Agents always run inside Docker containers for real workflows. Never run cloche-agent directly on the host - that bypasses the isolation model. CLOCHE_RUNTIME=local is for development and tests only.
Container seeding takes a clean git snapshot of the project; uncommitted files are invisible inside the container. One container per workflow run, shared by all steps with the same container id.
Container network access is allowlisted via network_allow; a step needing extra hosts declares a step-level container block rather than widening the workflow default.
Every declared step result must be wired; parse-time validation rejects unwired results, orphaned steps, and missing entry points.
A step must have exactly one of prompt, run, workflow_name, or poll - step type is inferred from the field present, and declaring more than one is a parse error.
Workflow names are project-unique identifiers across all .cloche files; the same workflow name appearing in two files is an error.
parked, done, and abort are reserved result names - steps cannot declare them in results or wire them as their own outcomes.

Prompt templates use double-brace directives: {{ $name }} for built-in or KV lookup, {{! cmd }} for shell stdout, {{@ path }} for file contents. Single-brace {task_description} placeholders are deprecated.
Any unresolvable template directive must fail the step before the agent is invoked - never send a prompt with unresolved placeholders to an LLM.
File contents and shell output injected into prompts are inserted literally and never re-templated.
KV values are capped at 1 KB; larger data goes into files under temp_file_dir with the file path stored in the KV store instead.
Built-in template variables such as task_id and run_id shadow KV keys of the same name; workflow authors cannot override built-ins with cloche set.
Use cloche poll or poll steps for waiting on external state; never busy-wait with sleep loops in scripts.
Poll and skip scripts run many times over a step's lifetime; any side effect such as posting a comment or creating a ticket must be guarded to run at most once, typically via a KV flag.
Check cloche status before modifying bead tasks - the daemon claims open tasks within seconds of creation, so unguarded bd updates race the orchestrator.
A stale claimed task, meaning in_progress with no active run, is reset with the release-task workflow rather than by editing tracker state directly.
After restarting the daemon, verify port 8080 actually bound - a stale cloched process can hold the port and the web dashboard silently fails to bind with no retry.
Run results are extracted to git branches named cloche/<attempt>-<container>; merges happen on the host from daemon-created worktrees, never inside the container.
The codebase is a single Go module; new commands are added as subcommands of the four existing binaries rather than as new binaries.
Every step gains an implicit token-limit result routing to abort; long-running agent steps should set explicit token budgets rather than relying on the 500k default.
Host workflow scripts always execute from the main git worktree, even when the project directory is a linked worktree on another branch.

queries.text: Cut a new release of cloche
Add a --json output flag to the status subcommand
The web UI stopped loading after I restarted the daemon
Remove the deprecated single-brace placeholder support from prompt assembly
Add support for a new sandbox provider besides Docker
Why doesn't the agent see the file I just created in .cloche/overrides?
Write a script that waits for CI to go green before merging
Pass a large JSON report from the review step to the summarize step
Mark the stuck ticket as open again
Let one step download packages from npmjs.org
Add a new step outcome called parked to the fix step
Inject the current git branch name into the implement prompt
The agent ran out of budget halfway through the refactoring task
Combine the results from the container run into main
